{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOUDROfM8AAAABiqQ3kw", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BlR_zzhMA17I", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BlR_z", "number": 405, "title": "Allow ordinary macOS text input when Accessibility editing metadata is unavailable", "body": "## Problem

Following merged PR #404 (#403), the user reports the actual error:

> Focus an editable text field that exposes Accessibility editing and try again.

The tested application/field was not specified in the report. Do not invent a reproduction target or assume the local app revision. The same message exists in current main at [a0119ff](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/commit/a0119ff04aeccad4c4b8338037d20ceb0e0f845a), in [desktop/mac-target.m](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/a0119ff04aeccad4c4b8338037d20ceb0e0f845a/desktop/mac-target.m).

Although #404 removed application-name allowlists, the new native Unicode input fallback still requires Accessibility to positively identify an editable field. In particular, captureTarget() rejects missing AXFocusedWindow/AXFocusedUIElement; editMethod() (approximately lines 49–81) rejects roles outside AXTextField/AXTextArea/AXComboBox and fields without a writable AXValue or affirmative AXEditable; check() rejects Unavailable before native input is attempted. These conditions are not equivalent to whether an application accepts ordinary typing/paste. Custom editors and applications with incomplete Accessibility information can be rejected even when a user can type in them normally. The error is a target rejection, not necessarily a permissions error.

## Expected outcome

Make macOS desktop dictation behave like ordinary user-initiated text input into the current application. **Do not require positive proof of Accessibility text editability as a prerequisite for normal native keyboard input or paste.** Accessibility editing is an optional insertion optimization and a useful source of focus/protection information, not a universal capability gate.

- Prefer a suitable existing direct edit when reliably available; otherwise provide a practical standard native input/paste path using normal OS authorization. Missing/unsupported AX role, AXEditable, writable AXValue, selection attributes, or focused element/window attributes must not by themselves be treated as proof that text entry is impossible. Distinguish explicit evidence of a disabled, read-only, or secure target from unknown/incomplete metadata. If exact field identity is unavailable, use the best available normal OS focus/application/window information; stop on observed target changes. Do not reject an entire application solely for incomplete Accessibility support.
- Evaluate conventional clipboard + Cmd+V as used by existing dictation applications (see #401 and #403) as well as the existing Unicode keyboard method. Reuse existing code where appropriate. Do not create a new app allowlist, role allowlist that defeats the fallback, per-app compatibility mode, or a new confirmation/warning just because the target is untested or exposes incomplete AX metadata. No extension, DOM injection or debugging connection in production.
- Maintain explicit user initiation, OS permissions, application/window binding and field identity when available, checks before dispatch, cancellation on observed focus change, ordered at-most-once output, no app-generated form submission or arbitrary commands, and no knowingly targeting protected/password/read-only controls. Respect secure-input indications and actual OS restrictions. Do not circumvent security protections. If safe ordinary input is genuinely unavailable, report that actual reason. A native input method cannot guarantee that every target consumes the text; preserve native editing semantics and document limitations. The already accepted residual in-flight focus race remains nonblocking.
- If using clipboard paste, preserve existing clipboard contents where feasible, guard against overwriting a subsequent user copy, serialize writes, and do not blindly retry after ambiguous dispatch. Do not silently transform text beyond necessary native input semantics or add speculative safeguards that block normal usage.
- Replace misleading Accessibility-editing error wording with concise actionable errors only for real failure conditions (e.g. missing OS authorization, lost focus, known protected target, or actual input failure). No warning merely for lacking direct Accessibility editing.
- Keep scope focused on the reported macOS failure. Preserve the existing shared desktop architecture and Linux implementation. Do not require exhaustive compatibility across all apps or OSs.

### Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Deterministic tests prove that an ordinary focused target with missing AXEditable, unsettable AXValue, an unfamiliar/custom role, or incomplete AX field information is not automatically refused; the standard input fallback can dispatch text under the revised policy. Exercise missing field/window metadata where ordinary OS targeting remains available.
- [ ] Retain representative tests for known protected/disabled/read-only targets, missing permissions, observed focus changes, cancellation, ordered deliveries, and no duplicate retry. Update obsolete tests that equate unknown AX metadata with a noneditable target. Test clipboard preservation if paste is selected.
- [ ] Build and launch the macOS package; run applicable permission-independent tests. Keep native cross-app tests optional when OS permissions are unavailable, with results accurately reported. No user/manual testing or exhaustive app verification is a merge/closure gate. Do not claim the user's particular app was verified if it was not identified.
- [ ] Update the desktop guide and PR with the behavior change, remaining genuine limitations and brief optional manual test steps. Do not expand the task into a search for a perfect universal editing API.

## Required post-merge verification

None. Optional user verification is not a closure condition.

## Context

Follow-up to #401, #403 and merged #404, based on the user's actual error report on November 26. Follow [development flow](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/docs/development-flow.md) and [review guidelines](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/docs/review-guidelines.md).
